events.title: C programming language takes shape at Bell Labs
events.summary: Dennis Ritchie evolved C from B during 1971–73; 1972 was the most creative period for the language and first compiler.
events.about: C is a systems language — close to the machine, but portable. Used to write operating systems (Unix/Linux kernels), databases, embedded firmware, game engines, and anything that needs speed and direct memory control. C still underpins most OS and runtime code today.

narrative.whyChosen: C became the systems language of Unix and later the foundation for C++, Objective-C, Go, and much of modern infrastructure.
narrative.whyImportant: It added a practical type system to B and enabled rewriting Unix in a portable high-level language.
narrative.problemSolved: B was too limited for the PDP-11 byte architecture and growing Unix kernel needs.

events.title: First Prolog interpreter at University of Marseille
events.summary: Alain Colmerauer and Philippe Roussel implemented the first Prolog in fall 1972 — logic programming as Horn-clause theorem proving with backtracking.
events.about: Prolog programs are facts and rules; the engine searches for proofs by unification and backtracking. Used in expert systems, natural-language tools, and symbolic AI. SWI-Prolog, GNU Prolog, and Warren's WAM influenced compiler design far beyond logic programming.

narrative.whyChosen: Prolog was the first widely used logic programming language and parent of most modern Prolog systems.
narrative.whyImportant: It showed declarative rules could drive real applications — from machine translation research to industrial expert systems.
narrative.problemSolved: Colmerauer's team needed one engine for both natural-language parsing and automated reasoning without separate theorem provers.
